headline: Americans embrace electric vehicles in historic shift
meta_description: More than half of Americans now more open to buying electric cars than a year ago, as public charging confidence jumps dramatically.
summary_short: More than half of Americans show increased openness to electric vehicles. Public charging confidence surged from 28% to 47%.
body:
More than half of Americans are now more open to buying an electric car than they were a year ago, signaling a major shift in consumer attitudes toward cleaner transportation.

The change extends beyond purchasing intent. Positive views of public charging infrastructure have jumped significantly, climbing from 28% to 47%—a jump that reflects growing confidence in the networks that make electric vehicle ownership practical for everyday drivers.

This momentum suggests that as Americans witness expanding charging options and accumulating real-world experience with electric vehicles, their reservations are giving way to genuine consideration. The data points to a tipping point where electric cars are moving from niche interest to mainstream conversation.
quick_facts: More than half of Americans more open to buying EVs than one year ago
Public charging positive views jumped from 28% to 47%
Survey shows major shift in American consumer attitudes toward electric vehicles
